items.title: Charter Revenue Declines Again as Subscriber Slide Continues
items.summary: Competition from fixed wireless and fiber connection services has been eating into the company’s home-internet subscriber base.

items.title: Booz Allen Profit, Revenue Falls Despite Accelerating Demand
items.summary: Booz Allen Hamilton reported lower fiscal first-quarter profit and revenue, but the company maintained its outlook and said it is seeing accelerating demand across parts of the business.

items.title: American Express Sales, Profit Rise on Higher Card Member Spending
items.summary: The credit-card company posted higher sales and profit in the second quarter, thanks to higher spending among its credit card members.

items.title: FactSet (FDS) Expands Insurance Reach As Curi Adopts Its Portfolio Analytics Suite
items.summary: FactSet Research Systems (NYSE:FDS) expanded its footprint in the insurance sector as Curi Holdings adopted its Portfolio Analytics Suite. The agreement centers on FactSet’s analytics and data aggregation tools for portfolio and risk management across Curi’s investment operations. The move highlights insurance client interest in integrated, front to back solutions for data, portfolio analysis, and risk oversight. items.title: SAP Stock Jumps as Earnings Beat Eases AI Fears
items.summary: Shares of  SAP  were rising on Friday as the German tech company shook off concerns about its software business with a better-than-expected quarterly earnings report.  The print indicated that artificial-intelligence tools and hardware spending aren’t replacing SAP, which offers cloud services and operations software for enterprises.  SAP posted earnings of €1.89 ($2.15) a share in the second quarter, up from €1.45 last year and above analysts’ consensus estimate of €1.68, per FactSet.

items.title: Edwards Lifesciences Narrows Full-Year Sales Outlook After Second-Quarter Growth
items.summary: The medical-technology company said it now expects sales of $6.6 billion to $6.9 billion for the full year, raising the bottom end of its prior range of $6.5 billion to $6.9 billion.

items.title: T-Mobile’s Churn Problem: Why Great Earnings Can’t Mask Saturated Mobile Markets
items.summary: T-Mobile US  stock was sliding on Thursday after the wireless carrier reported softer-than-expected second-quarter revenue, overshadowing an earnings beat.  T-Mobile reported adjusted earnings of $2.99, as revenue climbed 7.9% from a year ago to $22.8 billion.  Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.54 a share on revenue of $22.9 billion, per a FactSet poll.
